headline: Trump called anyone saying artificial intelligence, not superintelligence, the enemy.
body: The US president posted it a week after ordering federal agencies to use his term. Asked in parliament, Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said Japan keeps saying AI for now.

headline: Elon Musk accused Indian tycoons of blocking Starlink; India's government denies it.
body: Musk, who runs SpaceX and its Starlink satellite internet, says Starlink has waited five years. India's ministry says Starlink and two rivals all await security clearance, calling the claim baseless.

headline: OpenAI told investors its yearly sales pace is $20 billion below what it said before.
body: An unnamed source says the gap comes mostly from comparing OpenAI with rival Anthropic. Anthropic counts cloud partner sales, OpenAI does not; a pace is monthly sales times twelve.

headline: The World Trade Organization doubled its 2026 trade growth forecast on AI demand.
body: Trade in AI goods like chips and servers rose two thirds from January to June. They made almost half of all trade growth, offsetting damage from the Middle East war.

headline: AI firm Anthropic now scans open-source code, readable by all, for flaws for free.
body: Projects that opt in get scans by its strongest AI; nobody checks the flaw reports. Anthropic says some reports may be wrong; some projects already drown in AI bug reports.

headline: OpenAI says it shut down Russian and Iranian groups using ChatGPT for fake writers.
body: The Russian-linked group invented a think-tank head; the Iran-linked one planted almost 100 articles. The articles ran under fake journalists' names; OpenAI names no government agency behind either group.

headline: Oracle is trucking natural gas to its AI data centres while it waits for pipelines.
body: Trucked gas ran a Utah site a year and now feeds a Texas OpenAI campus. Analysts put trucked gas at about four times the usual price; Oracle did not comment.

headline: Humanoid robots directed traffic and guided tourists in a trial in Hangzhou, China.
body: Only the maker, Chinese robot firm Deep Robotics, describes the trial of its DR02 robots. The firm says they handled busy crossings in rain, to free staff for tasks needing judgment.

headline: Walmart's warehouse robots break down too often and cannot handle its big boxes.
body: After a decade, Walmart is still automating most of its roughly 200 US warehouses. Executives say fewer warehouse workers will be needed in time, without layoffs.

headline: Google unveiled its new top AI model, Gemini 4 Argon, first for security experts.
body: Trusted experts get it without Google's usual cyber limits; paying developers follow after safety tests. Google claims top scores in coding, finance, law and security, from its own tests.

headline: Scientists say AI firm Anthropic overstated its find of a possible gene-editing tool.
body: Anthropic said last month its AI found a DNA pattern that may edit genes. Copenhagen researcher Mario Rodríguez Mestre says his unpublished work shows it; he cannot prove copying.

headline: USA Today's publisher sued OpenAI, saying it copied hundreds of thousands of stories.
body: The publisher and its local papers say OpenAI trained AI on their articles without asking. They seek over $250 million; The New York Times also sues; OpenAI had not responded.

headline: A Google chatbot questioned patients before urgent visits and needed no safety stop.
body: Boston hospital doctors watched all 98 completed chats live and never had to step in. The study, paid by Google's parent, tested only safety, not whether patients got better.

headline: A US charity plans to record Gaza classrooms and have AI flag 'hateful' speech.
body: Dr David Hasan, founder of the charity Gaza Children Village, described the plan last month. A board member and a partner aid group raised privacy concerns; families may not know yet.

headline: A Colombian streamer's own robot whacked him on the head during a livestream.
body: Streamer Westcol turned his back while rehearsing a dance with the robot on air. He says it cost about $100,000; in earlier tests it kicked a display case apart.

headline: Google showed a Gemini AI helper for firms that works across apps, now in testing.
A humanoid shop robot shown in Tokyo could stock Japanese convenience stores from 2027.
US Democratic senators say some tech giants mislead on AI data centre costs and jobs.
San Francisco rents rose a quarter, blamed on the AI boom; eviction notices rose 44%.
AI investors now want results, not promises, after OpenAI's lower sales figure.
body: OpenAI's sales pace came in lower; data-centre firm Firmus dropped its share sale. Watch if OpenAI raises money at a $1.4 trillion value; not financial advice.
